summary: Deschutes NF lookout built 1933 as a 40-ft L-4 tower; later removed or destroyed. Little remains at the summit, per a visitor guide.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 40-foot round timber tower
facts.status_note: Tower and cab are gone; the Willhite guide says not much remains at the summit
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Deschutes National Forest

access.note: On national forest land beside the Cascade Lakes Highway; Willhite describes an easy drive-up in high-clearance 4WD when the road has been brushed out

visit.trail_note: A decent road takes you about halfway up; the rest needs high clearance and a road that has been brushed out

events.note: 40-foot round timber tower with an L-4 cab, per the register and the Kamstra, Kemnow and Willhite pages
The L-4 lookout house (cab) completed; a 16-by-18 garage also built
Hazard sticks, balanced scales and wind recording instruments installed
Abandoned campfire blamed for one of two fires from the east shore of Davis Lake; spotted and brought under control by the lookout
Tom Morris named as the Davis Mountain lookout in August 1950
Register says later removed; Kamstra's page says later destroyed; neither gives a date
Registered April 25, 2011; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Most pages give 1933 for the tower. Kemnow's page also quotes a November 1932 report that the tower was complete then, with the lookout house still to be erected. The story keeps 1933 and reports the 1932 account.
The register says the tower was removed and Kamstra's page says it was destroyed. Neither gives a date or method, so the story reports the disagreement.

sources.title: Davis Mountain Lookout - Cascade Lakes Highway

notes_for_editor: Register and firelookout.com disagree on removed vs destroyed; no removal date in any source. The only account of what remains is Willhite's 'Not much remains' and two photo captions (footing, footing with eyebolt). Access is inferred from Willhite's drive-up description; no current closure notice was found. Kemnow's page quotes a 1932 Bend Bulletin report, so the 1932/1933 build date is noted in the story. No staffing after 1950 is documented.
